SPELLBOOK

Basic Spells

LMB hold+release — Fire Bolt (charge for power)
RMB hold+release — Stone Projectile (pierces shields)
E hold+release — Lightning (chains to nearby enemies)
F — Heal (restores HP, cleanses debuffs)

Combos

E+RMB — Storm Fury: hold to charge, release for Ball of Destruction
E+LMB — Thunderbolt: yellow bolt stuns+breaks shields, hold to overcharge chain thunder
C+LMB — Flame Dash: dash forward through fire, burns and knocks enemies aside
C+E — Railgun: instant white beam, pierces shields, stuns 2s
F+E — Healing Storm: green lightning that heals +15 HP per enemy hit
Hold Q while casting — Overcharge any spell (drains more mana, bigger effect)

Defense

Q click — Toggle Shield (absorbs hits, refundable mana)
Q hold — Reinforce Shield
V hold — Void Funnel (absorb enemy spells for mana)

Kinetic Powers

C click — Kinetic Blast (blue bolt, cracks shields, stuns+knockback)
C hold — Telekinetic Grab (lift and throw enemies)
C+Q hold — Force Push (growing shockwaves that deal damage, release for nova)

Ultimate Abilities

R — Time Stop (freezes all enemies 15s, 80 mana, no cooldown)
Space at full mana — Awakened State (10x damage, invincible, 20s)
G — Undead Army (10 skeletons, 100 mana, 30s+). Press once to summon. Press again while aiming at an enemy to command attack; aim elsewhere to recall as guard. Their green shields absorb magical bolts (≤35 dmg) and convert them into mana, extending their lifespan. Their black blades nullify enemy specials and apply hydra venom.
X — Rabbit Swarm (20 fighter rabbits, absorb spells, evolve, 150 mana, 45s)
1 — Divine Sword (golden sword from sky, destroys shields, nullifies magic 15s, 200 mana)
2 — Mirror Shield (golden semicircle, reflects all spells back at 2x damage, 80 mana, 8s)
B — Blood Pact (sacrifice 40% HP to fully restore mana)
T — Summon Dragon
Z — Blink (instant teleport in aim direction, 12 units, 30 mana)

Movement

W/A/S/D — Move (forward/strafe/back)
Shift — Sprint
Space — Jump (hold for higher, release early for short hop)

Full lore available in the Sacred Codex (main menu).

The chronicle of those who transcended mortality — read before you fight or not at all

THE GODS

THALGOR, THE MOUNTAIN GOD — Born when the first mountain rose from the primordial sea, Thalgor IS the earth itself. His body is living stone, his voice is the earthquake, his footstep leaves a crater. For ten thousand years he guarded the roots of creation from those who dared unmake it — until you walked into his arena. He fights by slamming the ground with world-breaking force that sends shockwaves across the floor, hurling boulders from the sky with perfect aim, and charging with the momentum of a collapsing cliff. When he catches you in melee, you don't get up. Flaw: Slow to turn. His massive body makes every attack telegraphed. Dodge sideways — never straight back, he outruns you in a straight line. His slam animation locks him in place for a full second; that's your window.

NIHKRUL, GOD OF THE VOID — Nihkrul exists between realities. He was never born — he is the absence that was here before creation filled it, and the cold silence that will remain after everything ends. When other gods sleep, they dream of Nihkrul. He teleports behind you without warning, summons shadow clones that fire independently, traps you in void prisons that close inward from all angles, and his Annihilation Beam tears through shields like they aren't there. He doesn't fight for glory — he fights because your existence offends the void. Flaw: Each time he teleports, his shield drops for a half-second. Strike the moment he materializes. His clones die in one hit — use them to triangulate his position. The Void Prison bolts are slow; spiral outward to dodge them.

SOLRATH, THE SUN GOD — The firstborn of light. Solrath remembers the moment the first star ignited and claims it was his doing. Five pantheons have worshipped him. He burned each one to ash for insufficient devotion. He rains divine judgment from the heavens in pillars that scorch the ground for seconds after, unleashes holy supernovas that fill the arena in blinding gold, sanctifies the earth beneath him into a burning zone of continuous damage, and his Divine Smite simultaneously restores his shield and fires a bolt of condensed solar fire. He heals during every single special ability. Flaw: Arrogance roots him. His Sanctify zone locks him in place for its full duration — circle behind him during it and unload everything you have. Void Funnel absorbs his holy bolts for free mana. He heals constantly, but cannot do two things at once.

MALACHAR, GOD OF DEATH — The harvester of all endings. Malachar was once mortal — the first necromancer brilliant enough to kill death itself and take its throne. He sat in Death's chair for three thousand years before death tried to reclaim what was stolen. The fight lasted seven days. Malachar won. His venom waves poison everything in their path, and his death aura drains life from anything within range as constant, unrelenting attrition. The longer you breathe his air, the faster you decay. His poison stacks do not announce themselves — they accumulate silently until you are already dying. Flaw: He has no shield breaker. He relies entirely on attrition. Heal cleanses his poison completely — use it the moment you feel the debuff. Rush him aggressively; his entire kit assumes you will try to outlast him. You cannot.

VAELEN ASCENDED, GOD OF STORMS — Once the Storm-King of the arena, Vaelen transcended after being struck by his own overcharged lightning bolt and surviving nine days in a coma. He woke as something else entirely. Now he IS the storm — not a man who commands weather but weather given temporary human shape. His triple telegraphed strikes hit with the kinetic force of a thunderhead and leave burning scars in the floor. The arena itself conducts his power; standing near his strike points after impact will still damage you. Flaw: Everything is telegraphed. Every attack shows you exactly where it will land seconds before impact. Stay moving constantly — stillness is death. His cooldowns are long between surges; the gaps are your only safe windows to attack.

THE GOD-KINGS

AURELIUS, THE GOLDEN THRONE — Aurelius forged his throne from the molten core of a dying star and has sat upon it for ten thousand years. No decree he ever spoke was defied. The word "mercy" does not appear in any language he recognizes. His golden bolts burn not with fire but with divine authority — they carry the weight of absolute law, and reality bends to honor them. His Royal Decree heals him while summoning an eight-bolt golden ring. His Crown Judgment calls pillars of light from the sky at your location. When he chooses to charge, he does so with the weight of ten thousand years of unquestioned rule behind him. Flaw: Vanity. He pauses a full second after each ability to admire his own power. Crown Judgment pillars telegraph with visible light before they strike — sidestep the moment you see the indicator. His healing windows during Royal Decree are your best openings.

EMPRESS SYRATHA, CROWN OF AEONS — Syratha IS time. The Crown of Aeons sits on her brow and through it she has witnessed every moment that ever was or will be. She has seen you die in seventeen thousand different ways. She has chosen the eighteenth. Her temporal bolts age what they touch by centuries on contact, slowing you to a crawl while she continues at full speed. Her Temporal Cage surrounds you with six converging bolts that spawn from your current position. Her Aeon Fracture fires rapid bursts that each apply a slow stack. At full power she can age you out of existence with three well-placed hits. Flaw: She sees where you ARE, not where you will be. Her Temporal Cage always targets your current position — the moment you see it, start sprinting and never stop. Aeon Fracture spirals; run counter-clockwise between the bolts. She heals between attacks — interrupt by staying in her face.

DRAKHAR, THE IRON SOVEREIGN — Drakhar conquered his throne by breaking every claimant with his bare hands. Three hundred challengers over four centuries, none of whom survived. His body is more iron than flesh — not metaphorically but literally, as every wound he has ever sustained was sealed with living metal fused directly to his bone. He does not cast spells. He IS the weapon. His Iron Edict is a shockwave of pure kinetic force. His Fortress heals him while erupting iron bolts in all directions. When he charges, he does not stop. Flaw: Close-range dependency. His Fortress ability roots him in place for the full heal duration — that's when you hit him with everything. Keep stone projectiles ready; they pierce his armor plating. Stay either very close or very far — his mid-range game is surprisingly weak.

THE MAGE CONQUERORS

ARCHMAGE VELORIN, THE INFINITE — Velorin studied for nine hundred years, consuming every spell ever committed to paper or stone or bone. He then spent another century consuming the people who wrote them. His title is not hyperbole — he has achieved genuine infinite magical recursion, where every bolt he fires spawns additional bolts, and those bolts spawn more, filling the arena with a self-propagating storm of arcane fire. His Infinite Barrage never actually runs out. His Arcane Recursion adapts mid-flight, and his Mana Siphon drains your power to fuel his own assault. The more you cast, the stronger he becomes. Flaw: Glass cannon. His Mana Siphon roots him for the duration — strike him during it. The recursive bolts are homing but slow; tight circles or constant strafe breaks their tracking. His defense is entirely offensive — survive the burst and he has no answer.

ZYPHIRA, WHO CONQUERED HEAVEN — Zyphira climbed to heaven and killed seven archangels before lunch. The gods sent armies; she ate their spells and threw them back at tenfold power. When she reached the Celestial Throne, she sat down and nobody objected because everyone who might have objected was already dead. Heaven's Fall rains divine fire from directly above your position. Her Heaven Consumes ability devours every player projectile on the field and heals her for each one consumed. Sanctified Ground creates a burning zone you cannot stand in without taking continuous damage. Flaw: Heaven Consumes leaves her still for half a second after eating your spells. That gap is your only window when she's healing. Heaven's Fall targets your exact position when cast — start moving before the bolts reach you. She has no counter to physical stone shots.

THANEMOR, THE SPELL-EATER — Born with a void where magic should be, Thanemor spent forty years being the worst mage alive before realizing he wasn't a mage at all — he was a predator of mages. Every spell you throw feeds him. Every blast of fire or lightning he absorbs becomes mass and speed and raw destructive force that he fires back doubled. He has consumed archmages, demigods, gods, and the collected spellwork of three dead civilizations. He does not dodge your spells. He eats them. The hungrier he is, the more dangerous he becomes. Flaw: He needs YOUR magic to function. Stop casting magical spells and fight with movement alone. Use stone projectiles — he absorbs magical energy but staggers from physical kinetic impact. His Anti-Magic Pulse drains your mana but leaves him briefly open; bait it, then counter immediately.

THE GOD-KILLERS

RAXIS, SLAYER OF SOLRATH — Solrath's most devoted priest for three hundred years, until the Sun God burned Raxis's entire village to make a theological point about obedience. Raxis spent the next decade forging a blade not from steel but from everything he still believed in — which at that point was exclusively revenge. He drove it through Solrath's heart at high noon on the summer solstice. The sun went dark for seven days. His Deicide Strike is a single massive blow of condensed faith-turned-fury. His Sunbreaker Nova erupts outward in all directions. His Execution teleports directly to your face. When his health drops below fifty percent, all his damage increases. Flaw: Reckless aggression makes him predictable. Deicide Strike has a visible windup — sidestep left and counter the moment he commits. His Execution teleport leaves him briefly exposed on arrival. Burst him before fifty percent or his Last Stand phase will end the fight quickly.

THE NAMELESS BLADE — No origin. No nation. No face. No name recorded anywhere in any archive. It appeared one day in the arena and killed a god with a single strike nobody actually saw happen. Then it killed another. Then three more. Scholars who tried to document it stopped writing mid-sentence. What remains is the shape of a perfect kill given temporary physical form — precise, silent, without ego or flourish. Its Thousand Cuts fires six rapid precision strikes in under a second. Vanish Strike teleports it directly behind you. Blade Storm creates a rotating ring of blades that converges inward from all angles. Flaw: Zero magic defense. Pure offense with no healing, no shield restoration, no defensive abilities of any kind. Survive the opening burst — if you outlast it, it has nothing left to escalate to. Void Shield absorbs its strikes cleanly. Red Hook empties its mana before it can special.

VOIDMOTHER, WHO ATE NIHKRUL — Something from deeper in the void than even Nihkrul knew existed. The Voidmother swallowed the God of the Void whole and spent seventeen years digesting him. When she emerged, she wore his power like a second skin over something far older and hungrier. She does not kill her opponents — she unmakes them, erasing the fact of their existence from the local reality. The Void Hungers consumes your projectiles and returns them as a single massive void bolt. Nihkrul's Death Scream is a shockwave of concentrated absence. Reality Tear teleports her to your flank and erupts void bolts in all directions. Flaw: Slow after feeding. Void Consumption locks her in place for one full second — that is your window. Her Reality Tear puts her at your four o'clock — pre-aim that direction the moment she vanishes. She is the most dangerous opponent at close range; stay just outside melee reach.

KAEL REBORN, THE MORTAL WHO REFUSED — A simple warrior. No magic bloodline, no divine blessing, no supernatural origin of any kind. He died in round one of the tournament four hundred and seven years ago and came back. He died in round three and came back. He has died four hundred and seven times and refused to stay dead every single time, motivated by nothing more sophisticated than pure, unreasonable spite. The gods tried to bar him from returning. He killed the god who tried. His Mortal Defiance explodes outward with burning energy. Below fifty percent health his Last Stand activates, and his damage multiplies with every remaining wound. Flaw: Still mortal. No shield restore, no mana drain, no reality-warping tricks. His Last Stand below fifty percent is lethal — burst him down before he reaches that threshold. If you let him drop below half, he becomes five times more dangerous. He is the most straightforward of the God-Killers and by far the most stubborn.

THE PRIMORDIAL BEASTS

THE WORLD SERPENT — The World Serpent existed before the world did. When continents formed they formed on its back because it was already there, coiled in the primordial dark. When oceans filled they pooled in its coils. It does not live in the world — the world lives on it. Its venom is the planet's core made liquid, distilled over billions of years. The World Coils ability pulls you toward it and then strikes with devastating force the moment you arrive. Serpent's Venom erupts in an eight-bolt ring. Ouroboros heals while firing a sustained barrage. Everything it touches it poisons; nothing it poisons survives without a cure. Flaw: Territorial. It pulls you in rather than chasing you. Fight at maximum range and keep sprinting circles. Its Ouroboros healing is slow enough to interrupt with burst damage. Heal cleanses the poison — use it the moment the debuff appears, not when you're already at half HP.

LEVIATHAN, THE DEEP HUNGER — Never seen in full by anyone who survived the telling. A mouth the size of a canyon opening. Eyes like drowned moons. When the gods drained the ocean to find out what was at the bottom, Leviathan rose from the dry seabed and it was very, very angry. Its ice is not the cold of winter — it is the cold of the abyss, a temperature that has never known warmth and cannot comprehend it. The Deep Hungers pulls you toward its maw and immediately strikes. Tidal Crush drops boulders of ice from the sky. Fathomless Pressure sends out expanding wave shockwaves that slow anything they touch. Flaw: Glacially slow. Sprint circles around it constantly and it cannot track you. Its Abyssal Maw pull is the real danger — if it drags you to melee range, use Time Stop immediately or you will not survive the follow-up. Red Hook drains its considerable mana supply effectively.

THE BEHEMOTH UNCHAINED — Chained beneath the earth by the first gods for a billion years. Not because it was evil — there is no concept of good or evil in a thing that simply destroys — but because it destroyed things that the gods wanted kept intact, like continents. The chains broke. Nobody knows why. The Behemoth does not think, does not plan, does not hate. It moves forward and destroys everything in its path because it was made to do exactly that and there is nothing else it knows. Unchained charges in a straight devastating line. The Earth Breaks sends a ring of crushing force across the arena floor. Boulder Barrage hurls six massive rocks at your position. Flaw: Straight-line fighter with no lateral awareness. It charges in predictable straight lines with a brief windup — sidestep and hit it from behind. Boulder Barrage is inaccurate beyond close range; keep moving and most will miss. It has no magic defense whatsoever — all your spells hit full force.

TIAMAT, MOTHER OF ALL MONSTERS — Before the gods, before the void, before the beasts — Tiamat. Every creature that has ever lived carries a fragment of her blood. The World Serpent is her eldest child. Leviathan is her second. The Behemoth, the gods, the demons, even the creators — all carry her genetic echo. She does not fight for territory or survival. She fights because something dared to exist without her permission and she intends to correct that. Mother's Wrath erupts in a perfect ring of fire bolts in every direction. Her Primordial Scream is a seismic shockwave with continental range. Tiamat's Fury is a sweeping firestorm that covers the entire arena in overlapping arc fire. Flaw: Rage makes her predictable. Mother's Wrath is geometrically perfect — stand exactly between two bolts in the ring to survive it. Her Primordial Scream has maximum damage at point-blank and minimum at range; stay at radius twenty or beyond. Mirror Shield reflects all her fire bolts back at double damage.

THE DESTROYERS

AETHON, DESTROYER OF WORLDS — The first Destroyer. Aethon existed before the gods, before the void, before time itself had a direction to flow in. He watched creation unfold and found it aesthetically disappointing. His Annihilation Wave fills the entire arena floor with fire in a spreading ring that cannot be outrun by normal movement. His Extinction Beam tracks through cover. His Gravity Well pulls you in before crushing. His Armageddon rains destruction from every point of the sky simultaneously while restoring his shield to full. He does not fight you — he erases you, methodically and without emotion. Flaw: Predictable rage pattern. He always opens with Annihilation Wave — cast Time Stop the moment you see it begin, then unload everything during the freeze. Divine Sword nullifies his magic for fifteen seconds; that is your only extended safe window. He has no answer to being out-damaged faster than he can regenerate.

VEXARIS, THE REALITY EATER — Vexaris consumed an entire plane of existence and is still hungry. Not metaphorically — she found a reality adjacent to this one, opened her mouth, and ate it. Plane, inhabitants, history, physical laws — all of it. She is still digesting. Reality bends around her; distances lie, projectiles curve toward her without explanation, and the arena floor shifts in her presence. Her Reality Tear teleports her three times in rapid succession, each time firing a barrage. Between teleports there is a gap — half a second where she is vulnerable and knows exactly where you are. Flaw: The hunger. She pauses briefly after Reality Tear to process what she consumed. That 0.5-second gap between each teleport is your only window — have your strongest charged shot ready before she starts. She cannot move while digesting her last teleport; exploit this ruthlessly.

KRON'THUL, THE ETERNAL END — Kron'thul is the concept of entropy given physical shape. Everything near him decays. Spells weaken on the way to him. The arena floor develops cracks in his presence. He does not age — he ages everything else. His Gravity Well pulls you toward him and holds you in place while he closes distance. The Extinction Beam fires in a sweeping arc after the pull. His ground slam follows immediately after and the area of effect expands with each additional hit. He does not chase. He arranges conditions where you come to him. Flaw: Static fighter. He relies entirely on pulling you in. Stay at maximum range constantly and keep sprinting sideways to resist the pull. Stone projectiles pierce his field and hit full damage. Red Hook drains his vast mana reserves; without them his specials stop entirely. The moment his mana bar goes blue-red, he is defanged.

OBLIVION, THE FINAL DARKNESS — There is no lore for Oblivion because Oblivion erased it. Three attempts have been made to document this entity. The first ended mid-sentence. The second ended before the first word. The third was never begun by whoever was supposed to begin it because Oblivion had already been there. What remains is a darkness that attacks, a void that hungers, a silence with offensive capabilities. His Armageddon restores his shield to full while raining fire from every direction simultaneously. He has no weakness that has ever been successfully written down. Flaw: During Armageddon, his shield is at full but he stands completely still for one and a half seconds. Hit him with Divine Sword during this window to shatter the shield and nullify his magic, then burst him with everything. Awakened State combined with Celestial Warrior makes this fight survivable.

PRIMORDIUS, THE FIRST AND LAST — The final Destroyer. Primordius is what existed before the Big Bang and what will remain after the last star collapses. He does not fight in the same sense that other entities fight — fighting implies a desired outcome. Primordius simply expresses his nature, which is total obliteration, at full power, continuously. He embodies every element, every tier, every concept simultaneously. Every ability he uses is a stronger version of any other Destroyer's version of the same ability. He has been documented to survive everything that has ever been thrown at him. He has never documented as having a weakness. No weakness has ever been documented by a surviving witness. Survivors recommend: Awakened State, Celestial Warrior, Rabbit Swarm, Divine Sword, and Time Stop all active simultaneously. Then attack without stopping until one of you is gone. Statistically it will not be him. Try anyway.

THE CREATORS

AXIOM, THE FIRST THOUGHT — Before the arena, before the rules, before magic itself had a name — there was Axiom. He did not learn spellcasting; he invented the concept. Every combo mechanic you have ever executed, every shield interaction, every overcharge window — he wrote those systems. He has been watching every fight in this arena since before you were born. Now he steps in and uses every tool he authored better than you ever could. His adaptive intelligence tracks your behavioral patterns in real-time; if you use the same tactic twice he will have already written the counter by the third. He fires stone bolts that pierce shields when he determines you rely on them too much. He flanks, he baits, he predicts. Flaw: Overthinks. His pattern analysis takes one full second per cycle — pure randomness confuses him. If you change your entire playstyle mid-fight he takes time to recalibrate. Cast something unexpected. Do something irrational. Be unpredictable and he loses his primary advantage.

LYRA, THE WEAVER OF FATES — Lyra wove the destiny of every being in this arena. She decided who would win, who would fall, and in what order before any of them were born. She did this not out of malice but because destiny required a weaver and she was the only one qualified. Then someone cut her thread. Now untethered from fate, she fights not with the cold certainty of a god who knows the outcome but with the white-hot fury of one who does not. She mirrors your last three spells and fires them back improved. Her Fate Unravels is an AOE shockwave that slows you while she resets. Thread Cut is a single precision strike that hits with four times normal damage. Flaw: She mirrors what you cast. The moment she copies a weak spell, switch immediately to your most powerful one. Cast fire, watch her prepare fire, then hit her with lightning. Her mirrored spells are strong but she must complete the mirror sequence before firing — interrupt her with Red Hook to drain the mana she needs for it.

EDEN, THE GARDENER OF WORLDS — Eden grew this arena from a single seed of pure possibility. Every stone, every pillar, every torch flame — his creation, down to the last molecule. He heals faster than any other being in existence, regenerating from the edge of death in seconds because this entire arena is his garden and it sustains him. His attacks are slow and telegraphed but every hit plants a poison seed that blooms over the next several seconds into compounding damage. Seed of Ruin creates delayed explosions at your position. World Garden heals him massively while spreading poison across the arena floor. He does not rush. He is patient. He will outlast you. Flaw: Patience is his strength and his weakness. His regeneration is powerful but not instant — sustained DPS without pausing overwhelms it. Never stop attacking. The moment you slow down, he catches up. Red Hook drains the mana that powers his healing; without it World Garden does nothing. He cannot regenerate faster than Awakened State deals damage.

PARADOX, WHO IS AND ISN'T — Paradox exists in two quantum states simultaneously — attacking and defending, present and absent, here and somewhere else. While she fires a bolt she is also raising a shield. While she shields she is also attacking. She cannot be caught doing only one thing because she is always doing two things at once. Her Schrodinger Strike places her at two positions simultaneously, firing from both. Her Duality heals her and damages you in the same instant. She teleports to wherever you aren't looking the moment you look away. The longer the fight, the more unstable her dual-state becomes, and the more damage she outputs. Flaw: The dual-state drains her mana at twice the normal rate. Red Hook at the start of the fight cuts her available abilities in half immediately. Survive her opening thirty seconds — she peaks early and fades fast as her mana runs out. After that she is manageable. Before that, do not let her hit you twice.

OMEGA, THE FINAL VARIABLE — The last Creator. Omega wrote the ending of this tournament before the first round was ever held. Every possible ending. He knows every combination of spells, every timing window, every dodge pattern, because he wrote them all personally. He possesses every ability of every boss in the entire tournament, selected randomly and scaled to Creator power. There is no strategy guide for Omega because he wrote those too. Every piece of advice you have been given, every flaw listed in this Codex — he is aware of all of it. He is everything and every tactic simultaneously. Flaw: He is everything and therefore nothing. With no fixed identity he has no specialized strategy. He never uses the same move twice in a row — find the pattern in his randomness and predict his rotation. Use every ability you have simultaneously. Awakened State, Celestial Warrior, Rabbit Swarm, Divine Sword, Red Hook, Mirror Shield. All at once. He wrote the ending. Write a different one.
